analysis:
This PR changes CI runner routing only. The macOS test jobs in .github/workflows/ci.yml (test-provider shards, summary, SDK, cluster checks, cluster shards, cluster GPU shards, cluster focused) now read `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[lane]`. The route job requests per-lane Darkbloom Sandbox grants and falls back to blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27. The accompanying docs (docs/developer/build.md) and changelog fragment describe this and remove the earlier statement that these jobs are never routed.

I examined the visible ci.yml head lines 1027-1217. The jobs use actions pinned to commit SHAs. Checkout sets persist-credentials false. Cache save is gated by SAVE_CACHES, which is limited to pushes on master and dev. The provider-test-gate still enforces the expected result for the cluster lanes by changes output. The docs state the route job uses a grant only when it repeats the exact Darkbloom labels, keeps the fallback on errors, and is skipped for fork PRs.

No provider runtime, WebSocket, attestation, App Attest, key or cache-storage code changed, so TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011 and the T-0xx provider entries are untouched.

Remaining questions for integration, all outside the visible evidence. The darkbloom-route.yml implementation and `scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py` are not in the supplied units, so I could not confirm label validation, or that the test which previously enforced literal labels was updated. The ci.yml patch excerpt is truncated, so the matrix `runs-on` expressions for the other jobs were not visible. Whether Darkbloom macOS runners are trusted for jobs that run PR code, and whether GitHub Actions cache entries saved from those runners cannot poison Blacksmith or master caches, relies on the existing push-only save rule and the plane's branch admission. Neither is verifiable here. This is a CI trust-boundary question, not a provider threat-model regression, and I am not reporting it as a finding.
